d: Becker is upset when a patient substitutes his Christian Science faith for medical treatment.

One of John's patients, a high school student named Brad, comes in for a physical and John learns that the guy's sexually active, but isn't practicing safe sex. John performs an HIV test on Brad and tries to convince him to begin practicing safe sex.
John's at the end of his rope with his hectic practice and makes a call, which Linda overhears, telling the person on the other end that he can't take another day.
John helps his elderly neighbor, Mrs. Firth, get into her apartment and she repays him by making homemade chicken noodle soup.

st: I’ve Got Friends I Haven’t Used Yet
d: Bob is distraught because a thirty-something guy at his gym died while on the treadmill, and he's certain that he's headed for the same fate.
When a customer leaves the diner because of John's cigarette smoke, Chris puts her foot down and tells him that it is now a "smoke-free" restaurant.
John arrives at the diner and announces that he has quit smoking.
John walks into the diner and sees Chris, Bob, and Jake standing around a booth.
Chris' ex-husband, Roger, is in town and comes to the diner to see her.
The fire marshal threatens to fine Chris for a faulty sprinkler system at the diner, but Chris flirts her way out of it.
John has a dream that he and Chris kissed each other. At the office, Linda is late and tells Margaret it's because her cab got hit by a runaway hotdog cart.

st: What’s Love Got To Do With It?
d: Highlights from last season include Chris and John exchanging "I love yous" as Chris is wheeled into surgery for an appendectomy.
At the diner, Jake bemoans his poor financial status, and Hector proposes that he participates in a drug-testing program to earn money.
Chris and John have their first impromptu date, but Chris wants something more formal before taking the relationship any further, and tells John so.
John takes Chris out for their first official date - to a cheap Chinese restaurant. both are excited about the possibility of their "first time."
As John and Chris get more serious in their relationship, Chris realizes that John is not as affectionate as she'd like him to be.
It's Thanksgiving and Chris wants to make dinner for John, who is totally against holidays.
At the diner, Hector tries to talk Jake into giving him money to invest in coffee futures, but Jake resists.
At the diner, Jake receives a letter and is shocked to find out that his late grandmother has left him $25,000.
Margaret tells John that a letter for a medical conference has arrived, but John scoffs, saying it's just an excuse for doctors to have a weekend in Las Vegas.
At the diner, Chris and Jake complain about the cold weather when John walks in, happy because it's cold and flu season, which means more patients.
At the diner, Jake is looking for someone to go downtown and pick up Stevie Wonder concert tickets for him with no luck.
Chris fears that John is going to break up with her after he invites her to dinner at a nice restaurant with no explanation.
An enraged and irascible Dr. John Becker (Ted Danson) enters the diner in his typical bad mood and sends the patrons fleeing.
Becker enters the diner to find Reggie in a rotten mood. After some prodding, she reveals that her ballplayer boyfriend just dumped her.
Becker is bombarded by sexual overtones throughout the day, beginning with a sensual dream that is interrupted by a neighbor's blaring music.

st: Take These Pills And Shove' Em
d: Becker arrives at the diner to find Reggie and Jake discussing their plans to take a sculpting class.
While Becker is at the diner with Jake and Reggie, an odd little man named Bob enters.
While railing on the evils of Beanie Babies, Becker gets annoyed when an overly friendly delivery guy named Todd stops by the diner.
Becker throws his back out at home while trying to close a stuck window.
Becker has a fear that midgets bring him bad luck and is spooked by the new water guy, who happens to be vertically challenged.
Becker promises a friend that he will write a medical article for him, but gets frustrated with numerous distractions.
Becker learns that an elderly patient, Mr. Fowler, has suffered from a heart attack and calls his daughter to tell her the bad news.
Becker yells at a woman for letting her child cry uncontrollably, then rants about her bad parenting skills.
Becker is outraged as he tells the gang at the diner that someone broke into his apartment and stole his computer.
Becker starts off the day in a cranky mood when he finds a stray cat in his office, which apparently crawled through a broken window.
Becker arrives at the office carrying the parking meter that ate his quarter.
